identification: American 'acorn' shelf clock, J.C. Brown / Forestville Manufacturing Co, Bristol (Forestville) Connecticut, c.1847-50. Laminated (bent-ply) rosewood/mahogany-look acorn-form case with laminated side arms and turned acorn finials on a stepped base, 65 cm high. Pointed upper door glass over a painted zinc dial (Roman numerals, pink-rose and gilt-leaf spandrels, no maker name visible on the dial in the photo), lower door with frosted/etched glass tablet in a feather-and-cross pattern with small coloured roundels. Inside: brass bell, brass-covered pendulum bob, and a torn printed paper label 'CLOCK MANUFACTORY / J. C. BROWN' with a woodcut vignette and text columns, the backboard paper mostly torn away. A brass fitting at the base, which could be the top of the detached fusees or a winding key. Looks period, not a modern copy, but this can't be confirmed from three 450x600 photos.

viewing_check: Open the lower door and photograph: (1) the movement. Originals have a lyre/pierced brass front plate signed 'Forestville Mfg Co' with TWO DETACHED FUSEES (cones) mounted in the base of the case, which is the single best test; a plain American spring or modern movement means a marriage or reproduction; (2) the full label and what is under the torn paper; (3) the dial bottom for a Forestville signature and whether it is repainted; (4) case construction, real laminated bentwood with old glue lines and shrinkage vs modern ply; (5) whether it runs and strikes, and that both acorn finials and the base are original. Measure the height (originals 24-25in / 61-64 cm without base variations).
